newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Afghan military chief retreats, avoids "bloodbath".
newsitem.headline: Afghan military chief retreats, avoids "bloodbath".

text.p: Afghanistan's deputy foreign minister said on Thursday that government troops were leaving Kabul to "avoid a bloodbath" with Islamic militants and that the president was considering transferring power.
Adbul Rahim Ghafoorzai told Reuters Television in an interview that President Burhanuddin Rabbani was on the outskirts of the capital and would decide on Friday about a "transfer of power."
The country's military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, had gone north of the city, taking with him jet fighters and other military hardware.

"The president is in the outskirts to the north and by tomorrow will announce his decision, whether to leave the capital," he said adding that the president would take the advice of other members of his high council.
He said he thought "there will be a transfer of power, to whom we do not know," adding that he would be consulting with members of his high council.
He said he hoped Afghan's former King, Zahir Shah, ousted in 1973 and now in Rome, would return to the country as even the Taleban would accept him in a leadership role.

Taleban sources in neighbouring Pakistan said the militia had seized the main government airbase at Bagram, 30 miles (50 km) north of Kabul after taking parts of the capital, including its abandoned Khwaja Rawash airport.
There was no immediate independent confirmation of these reports, but witnesses in Kabul said government forces appeared to be abandoning the capital they had vowed to fight to their death to defend.
The Taleban sources said the militia had also taken Kabul's Soviet-built Microrayon housing complex in the east and the diplomatic Wazir Akbar Khan district in central Kabul.
